items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: it was just about the time when Miles Davis came out here, because he was following Charlie Parker anywhere Charlie Parker went during that period

ctx.x: And Iggy Shavack(?), the bass player... Iggy was a very fine bassist on the scene at the time. He was one of the first guys that came through who really was singing on the bass, where the strings were singing, you know, around that time.

And during this time, it was just about the time when Miles Davis came out here, because he was following Charlie Parker anywhere Charlie Parker went during that period -- and Charlie stayed out here. In fact, later on we lived together at a place down on Vernon Avenue just east of Avalon -- Gene Montgomery, the tenor player. We were living in the Civic Hotel, and we decided to move into this house, and Charlie came in there to live with us. This was just about the latter part of 1945, while I was still…
Billy Byers was on the scene, the trombonist and arranger, and Warne Marsh used to come on the set and play.
